prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: COc1cc2c(cc1Cc1cccc(Cl)c1F)c(=O)c(C(=O)O)cn2[C@H](CO)C(C)C
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL3471

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of HIV1 integrase strand transfer activity
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of HIV-1 integrase assessed as inhibition of strand transfer activity using 32P-labeled DNA as substrate after 1 hr by gel-based assay in presence of Mg2+
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
INSUFFICIENT_INFO is not a valid response. You must commit to COMMENSURABLE or NOT_COMMENSURABLE.
If you lack direct evidence, make your best guess based on compound structure and target identity.
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.62, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 for HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibition with confidence score 9 against the same target, though Assay B specifies Mg2+ as the divalent cation; since both are strand transfer assays and the compound is a classic integrase strand transfer inhibitor with a metal-chelating pharmacophore, results under similar conditions are expected to agree reasonably well, but the specific mention of Mg2+ (vs potentially Mn2+ in Assay A) introduces some uncertainty."}
